title: Platform degradation simulation training curriculum
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview:
This curriculum defines a repeatable lab series and assessment for platform operators to learn how to detect, simulate, and remediate realistic degradation modes in the Redwood inference stack. The focus is on inference-specific failure classes (latency tail, KV cache thrash, model-variant fallout, and eviction storms) and on exercising cross-team runbooks (platform, serving-runtime, SRE).

Goals and learning objectives:
- Teach operators to map observability signals to root causes for LLM inference disruptions.
- Practice coordinated remediation (traffic steering, model swap, cache rebuild, tenant throttling).
- Validate dashboards, synthetic tests, and escalation paths used during incidents.
- Produce measurable improvement in mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for platform degradation incidents.

Audience:
- Platform operators, SREs, and on-call engineers who operate inference endpoints and GPU pools.
- Product/platform engineers who own rollout or model-variant fallback logic.

Prerequisites and setup summary:
1) Access: operators need "platform-operator" role and read/write to the synthetic-lab project namespace.
2) Environments: a dedicated lab region (eu-lab-1) with scaled-down GPU pool and an isolated tenant for load generation.
3) Baseline artifacts: a baseline dashboard (link below), traffic-replay assets, and a pre-seeded KV prefix cache snapshot.

Required dashboards and tools:
- Lab SLO dashboard (latency percentiles, token-cost, error-rate, model-variant-fallbacks).
- Cost & token breakdown per-request traces viewer.
- Incident runbook checklist (playback-able via the operator CLI).
- Synthetic load harness: lab-loader (Git repo: git://redwood/lab-loader).

Curriculum modules (4 weeks recommended, modular delivery):
Week 1 — Foundations and Signals
- Lecture: LLM-specific telemetry (prefix cache hit/miss, batch sizes, KV latency, model-switch counters).
- Workshop: interpret lab dashboard panels and map signals to the incident taxonomy.
- Assessment: identify root cause given 3 recorded incidents.

Week 2 — Cache & Batching Failure Modes
- Scenario lab: deliberate cache-shard desync and prefix eviction storm.
- Operator tasks: detect eviction spike, apply cache-prefetch policy toggle, and initiate cached-prefix reseed.
- Key checks: cache hit ratio improvement, token-cost delta, service CPU on inference hosts.

Week 3 — Model Variant and Fallbacks
- Scenario lab: deploy a model variant with increased generation latencies that triggers fallback flow.
- Operator tasks: observe fallback percentages, adjust routing policy, perform controlled model rollback.
- Validation: confirm fallback counts drop and p95 latency returns below SLO.

Week 4 — Multi-tenant Throttling and Degradation Containment
- Scenario lab: tenant spike that saturates GPU pools and causes soft-degradations for other tenants.
- Operator tasks: exercise tenant soft-quota enforcement, apply prioritized-tenant burst credits, and test eviction policy.
- Outcome: isolation preserves SLO for priority tenants while back-pressure is applied to lower tiers.

Lab scenarios and exercise matrix (table):
Scenario | Trigger | Primary SLO impacted | Operator action | Expected measurable result
---------|--------:|---------------------:|-----------------|--------------------------
KV eviction storm | Simulated cache corruption | p99 latency | Toggle cache-prefetch, reseed prefixes, monitor cache hit ratio | p99 latency reduces >30% within 10m
Model-variant latency | New model build with regressed kernels | p95 latency and error rate | Route traffic to stable variant, rollback model, open model-onboarding ticket | Fallback rate drops to <1% and p95 recovers
Tenant surge | Synthetic tenant traffic spike | availability and tail-latency for platform | Apply tenant throttling, activate burst-credit reconciliation | Priority tenant SLO preserved; overall throughput reduced
Routing split misconfig | Incorrect weight in feature flag | correctness and latency | Reconcile feature flags, run canary rollback, reweight traffic | Errors in canary drop, p95 stable

Runbook excerpt (operator checklist):
1) Triage: confirm alert on Lab SLO dashboard and annotate suspected failure class.
2) Contain: apply conserved traffic steering (mute non-critical regions / enable degraded routes).
3) Remediate: follow scenario play instructions (cache reseed, model rollback, tenant throttle).
4) Stabilize: observe 2x SLO window; if not recovered, escalate to Serving Runtime on-call.
5) Postmortem: create incident with evidence (traces, before/after metrics) and link to lab exercise ID.

Commands and snippets (lab tooling):
- Generate synthetic tenant spike:
```
lab-loader --tenant lab-tenant-42 --rps 1200 --pattern spike --duration 15m --seed 2026
```
- Toggle cache-prefetch feature flag for lab region (OPA CLI):
```
opa-cli set-flag --env eu-lab-1 --flag cache-prefetch-enabled --value false
```
- Rollback model variant via operator CLI:
```
redwoodctl models rollback --region eu-lab-1 --service inference-prod --target-variant stable-v1
```

Observability acceptance criteria (what to validate after each exercise):
- Alert reduction: active incident alerts should go from >1 to 0 within 15 minutes for contained scenarios.
- Latency improvement: p95/p99 reduce by target thresholds defined per scenario table.
- Token-cost: documented token-cost delta must be within allowed guardrail (no more than +10% for remediation actions).
- Audit trail: runbook steps and CLI commands used must be committed to incident timeline.

Assessment and certification:
- Each operator must complete three graded labs: one cache incident, one model-fallback incident, one multi-tenant containment.
- Passing criteria: successful remediation in under 25 minutes on average across the three labs, full runbook documentation, and verbal debrief.
- Certification: operators who pass receive the "Platform Degradation Responder (PDR)" badge in the internal learning system.

Post-lab retrospective template (to be completed after each game):
1) Summary of what happened and timeline.
2) What signals were most/least useful?
3) Runbook steps that worked / failed.
4) Dashboard gaps and instrumentation requests.
5) Follow-ups and owners (with target dates).

Metrics to track across training cohort (quarterly):
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for lab incidents.
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for each incident class.
- Percentage of labs that required escalation to serving-runtime team.
- Operator confidence score (post-lab survey).

Appendix A — Dashboard links and queries:
- Lab SLO dashboard: /dashboards/lab-slo-platform-2026
- Trace query example (token-cost attribution):
```
trace.query("service:inference AND tag:lab-tenant-42") | group_by(model_variant) | top(10, p95_latency)
```

Appendix B — Lab environment teardown checklist:
- Stop lab-loaders and verify zero synthetic sessions.
- Re-enable any disabled feature flags.
- Clear lab-only KV prefixes: `redis-cli --scan --pattern lab:* | xargs redis-cli del`.
- Ensure model traffic weights returned to production values.

Ownership and cadence:
- Curriculum owner: Platform Training Squad (owner: Asha Kapoor).
- Quarterly gamedays scheduled: first Monday of each quarter.
- Curriculum review: semi-annual or after any production incident that reveals gaps.

Related resources:
- Incident runbook library: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Operator onboarding pathway: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026
- Lab tooling repo: git://redwood/lab-loader

Notes and next steps:
- Pilot: run a pilot gameday with 6 operators in March 2026 and collect MTTD/MTTM baselines.
- Integrations: explore adding synthetic golden-metrics to the CI pipelines to detect subtle regressions earlier.

Authors and contributors:
- Curriculum authored by Asha Kapoor. Reviewed by Jonah Li, Priya Menon, and Derek Hale.
